subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: The Universal Joint: Bending the Drive
description: A quick, practical guide to The Universal Joint: Bending the Drive.

hook.text: A drive shaft must pass power around a bend. A rigid shaft can't do that.

buildup.text: A universal joint uses a cross-shaped spider between two yokes.

discovery.text: The spider lets the shafts meet at an angle while transmitting torque.

twist.text: A single U-joint causes speed fluctuations. Pairs cancel the pulsing out.

climax.text: Every rear-wheel-drive car uses U-joints in its driveshaft.

punchline.text: Bend the shaft and keep spinning — that's the U-joint's trick.

quiz.question: Why are universal joints usually used in pairs?
options: One joint handles torque while the other handles speed
A single U-joint causes speed variations that a second joint cancels
Two joints double the maximum angle the shaft can bend
